title: 🏛️ Exams 2006–2026 · linking words in exam texts ⭐⭐

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2023, technical) A text about Gilbert, a boy who wants to become a welder. Which word fits the gap?
"He wants to be a welder. ___, he lived in poverty with his grandmother in Spain."
questions.explanation: His wish (to be a welder) and his past (poverty) pull in opposite directions, so the second sentence needs a contrast word: "However". "So" and "Therefore" would say that poverty is the result of his wish, and "Besides" would add one more thing in his favour.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2026, general) A text about Prasiddhi, a twelve-year-old who plants trees across India. Which word fits the gap?
"___ many children her age are still learning the basics of biology, Prasiddhi is leading reforestation projects."
questions.explanation: The two ideas are opposites (children who are still learning, a girl who already leads projects), and "While" opens the first idea and takes a comma after it. "Therefore" gives a result, which is not the link. "However" also marks a contrast, but it stands between two sentences, not in front of a clause that depends on the next one.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2023, technical) A text about being green and protecting the earth. Which word fits the gap?
"It is true that pollution is a problem ___ the earth remains a glorious place that is ready for us to explore."
questions.explanation: The sentence admits that pollution is a problem and then opposes it with a positive fact: the link is contrast, so "but". "then" would put the two ideas in time order, and "or" would offer a choice between them.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2023, general) A pupil remembers a funny memory: a shoe fell from the sky and hit him in the face. Which word fits the gap?
"As my nose was bleeding, I rushed to the toilet. ___ a teacher caught me and sent me to the headmaster's office."
questions.explanation: He rushed to the toilet to clean himself, and what happened next went against what he wanted: a teacher caught him. That is a contrast, so "But". "After" and "Because" would leave an unfinished sentence, and "Besides" would add an extra fact instead of opposing the first one.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2020, general) A woman tells how her family came from Mexico to the United States. Which word fits the gap?
"I was thirteen years old ___ my father came to the US and mum stayed with my sisters and me back in Mexico."
questions.explanation: The gap introduces the moment of a single event, linked to her age: "when". "where" is for a place, and "while" is for something that goes on for some time at the same time as another action; the father arrived once.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2020, technical) A woman explains why she joined her partner's design company. Which word fits the gap?
"She thought the decision was easy as her background was already in art and as she holds a degree in three-dimensional design. ___, joining the family business would increase their financial security."
questions.explanation: Both sentences give reasons that make the decision easy: the second one only adds a reason, so the linker is "Besides" (and also). "But" and "However" would oppose the two reasons, as if the financial security were against the decision.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2019, technical) A text about Katie, who became a lorry driver. Which word fits the gap?
"It's a job made only for men. ___, Katie believes that there is no reason women can't do it."
questions.explanation: Katie's belief is the opposite of what people say, so the sentences are linked by contrast: "But". "And" would join two similar ideas, and "Because" would make her belief the cause of the idea that the job is for men.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2018, technical) A text about a father worried that his three children spend too much time online. Computers have just been mentioned. Which word fits the gap?
"His daughters have their own computers and his son, the youngest, uses the family desktop. ___, there are ipads and iphones."
questions.explanation: The sentence adds one more kind of device to the computers already listed: "Besides". "However" would oppose the two sentences, "So" would make the devices a result of the computers, and "Because" would make them a cause and leaves an unfinished sentence.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2013, technical) A short text about Jim, a painter who loses his ladder. Which word fits the gap?
"Jim is a painter. ___ he isn't working today because he hasn't got his ladder."
questions.explanation: We expect a painter to work, and the second sentence says the opposite: "But". "So" would say that his job is the reason why he is not working, and "Also" would add one more fact about his job. "But" is the only word that opposes the expectation.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2009, general) A text about Kayle, a pupil who had to change school after being hit. Which word fits the gap?
"___ Kayle had serious stomach problems, a girl at her school hit her in the stomach."
questions.explanation: "Although" opens a part that would make us expect the opposite of the main fact: knowing that Kayle had stomach problems, a girl hit her there all the same. "But" and "And" join two clauses in the middle of a sentence and cannot open a sentence that has a comma in the middle. (This linker is not in the course: the sentence shows how it works.)

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2007, unique) A woman tells how she changed her career as a secretary. Which word fits the gap?
"Two years later, however, she realised that she did not like being in an office. ___, she left and started looking for a different job."
questions.explanation: Leaving the office is the consequence of not liking it, so the gap needs a consequence word: "So". "However" and "Yet" mark a contrast, as if she had left although she liked her job.

questions.prompt:
(Exam 2006, unique) A text about two neighbours, Dave and Jenny, who have been close friends for years while Dave is moving to another city. Which word fits the gap?
"Dave and Jenny have been an important part of each other's lives; ___ it's difficult to say goodbye."
questions.explanation: Because they have been important to each other, saying goodbye is hard: the second part is a consequence of the first, so "so". "but" would oppose the two ideas, and "until" would give a time limit that the sentence does not need.
